The renv package helps you create reproducible environments for your R projects.
This vignette introduces you to the basic nouns and verbs of renv, like the user and project libraries, and key functions like `renv::init()`, `renv::snapshot()` and `renv::restore()`.
You'll also learn about some of the infrastructure that makes renv tick, some problems that renv doesn't help with, and how to uninstall it if you no longer want to use it.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-renv-verbs
#| fig.align: center
#| out.width: null
#| fig.alt: >
#|   A diagram showing the most important verbs and nouns of renv.
#|   Projects start with init(), which creates a project library using
#|   packages from the system library. snapshot() updates the lockfile
#|   using the packages installed in the project library, where restore()
#|   installs packages into the project library using the metadata from
#|   the lockfile, and status() compares the lockfile to the project library.
#|   You install and update packages from CRAN and GitHub using install()
#|   and update(), but because you'll need to do this for multiple projects,
#|   renv uses cache to make this fast.
#| fig.cap: >
#|   The most important verbs and nouns of renv, which you'll learn more
#|   about below.
#|   
knitr::include_graphics("renv.png", dpi = 144)
```

We assume you're already living a project-centric lifestyle and are familiar with a version control system, like Git and GitHub: we believe these are table stakes for reproducible data science.
If you're not already using projects, we recommend [Workflow: scripts and projects](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/workflow-scripts.html) from *R for Data Science*; if you're unfamiliar with [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and [GitHub](https://github.com/), we recommend [Happy Git and GitHub for the useR](https://happygitwithr.com).

## Libraries and repositories

Before we get into how renv works, you'll learn to fully understand two important pieces of R jargon: libraries and repositories.

A **library** is a directory containing installed packages.
This term is confusing because you write (e.g.) `library(dplyr)`, making it easy to think that you're loading the dplyr library, not the dplyr package.
That confusion doesn't usually matter because you don't have to think about libraries, simply installing all packages into a **system library**[^1] that's shared across all projects.
With renv, you'll start using **project libraries,** giving each project its own independent collection of packages.

[^1]: More precisely, there can be up to three system libraries: an (optional) **user** library, an (optional) **site** library, and a **default** library (where base R packages are installed).

You can see your current libraries with `.libPaths()` and see which packages are available in each library with `lapply(.libPaths(), list.files)`.

A **repository** is a source of packages; `install.packages()` gets a package from a repository (usually somewhere on the Internet) and puts it in a library (a directory on your computer).
The most important repository is CRAN; you can install packages from CRAN in just about every R session.
Other freely available repositories include [Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org), the [Posit Public Package Manager](https://packagemanager.posit.co), and [R Universe](https://r-universe.dev/) (which turns GitHub organisations into repositories).

You can see which repositories are currently set up in your session with `getOption("repos")`; when you call `install.packages("{pkgname}")`, R will look for `pkgname` in each repository in turn.

## Getting started

To convert a project to use renv, call `renv::init()`.
It adds three new files and directories to your project:

-   The project library, `renv/library`, is a library that contains all packages currently used by your project[^2]. This is the key magic that makes renv work: instead of having one library containing the packages used in every project, renv gives you a separate library for each project. This gives you the benefits of **isolation**: different projects can use different versions of packages, and installing, updating, or removing packages in one project doesn't affect any other project.
-   The **lockfile**, `renv.lock`, records enough metadata about every package that it can be re-installed on a new machine. We'll come back to the lockfile shortly when we talk about `renv::snapshot()` and `renv::restore()`.
-   A project R profile, `.Rprofile`. This file is run automatically every time you start R (in that project), and renv uses it to configure your R session to use the project library. This ensures that once you turn on renv for a project, it stays on, until you deliberately turn it off.

[^2]: If you'd like to skip dependency discovery, you can call `renv::init(bare = TRUE)` to initialize a project with an empty project library.

The next important pair of tools is `renv::snapshot()` and `renv::restore()`.
`snapshot()` updates the lockfile with metadata about the currently-used packages in the project library.
This is useful because you can then share the lockfile and other people or other computers can easily reproduce your current environment by running `restore()`, which uses the metadata from the lockfile to install exactly the same version of every package.
This pair of functions gives you the benefits of **reproducibility** and **portability**: you are now tracking exactly which package versions you have installed so you can recreate them on other machines.

Now that you've got the high-level lay of the land, we'll show a couple of specific workflows before discussing some of the reproducibility challenges that renv doesn't currently help with.

### Collaboration

One of the reasons to use renv is to make it easier to share your code in such a way that everyone gets exactly the same package versions as you.
As above, you'll start by calling `renv::init()`.
You'll then need to commit `renv.lock`, `.Rprofile`, `renv/settings.json` and `renv/activate.R` to version control, ensuring that others can recreate your project environment.
If you're using git, this is particularly simple because renv will create a `.gitignore` for you, and you can just commit all suggested files[^3].

[^3]: If you're using another version control system, you'll need to manually ignore `renv/library` and any other directories in `renv/`.

Now when one of your collaborators opens this project, renv will automatically bootstrap itself, downloading and installing the appropriate version of renv.
It will also ask them if they want to download and install all the packages it needs by running `renv::restore()`.

### Installing packages

Over time, your project will need more packages.
One of the philosophies of renv is that your existing package management workflows should continue to work, so you can continue to use familiar tools like `install.packages()`[^4].
But you can also use `renv::install()`: it's a little less typing and can install packages from GitHub, Bioconductor, and more, not just CRAN.

[^4]: Behind the scene, renv shims `install.packages()`, `update.packages(),` and `remove.packages()` to call the renv equivalents.
    Learn more in `?renv::load.`

If you use renv for multiple projects, you'll have multiple libraries, meaning that you'll often need to install the same package in multiple places.
It would be annoying if you had to download (or worse, compile) the package repeatedly, so renv uses a package cache.
That means you only ever have to download and install a package once, and for each subsequent install, renv will just add a link from the project library to the global cache.
You can learn more about the cache in `vignette("package-install")`.

After installing the package and checking that your code works, you should call `renv::snapshot()` to record the latest package versions in your lockfile.
If you're collaborating with others, you'll need to commit those changes to git, and let them know that you've updated the lockfile and they should call `renv::restore()` when they're next working on a project.

### Updating packages

It's worth noting that there's a small risk associated with isolation: while your code will never break due to a change in another package, it will also never benefit from bug fixes.
So for packages under active development, we recommend that you regularly (at least once a year) use `renv::update()`[^5] to get the latest versions of all dependencies.
Similarly, if you're making major changes to a project that you haven't worked on for a while, it's often a good idea to start with an `renv::update()` before making any changes to the code.

[^5]: You can also use `update.packages()`, but `renv::update()` works with the same sources that `renv::install()` supports.

After calling `renv::update()`, you should run the code in your project and verify that it still works (or make any changes needed to get it working).
Then call `renv::snapshot()` to record the new versions in the lockfile.
If you get stuck, and can't get the project to work with the new versions, you can call `renv::restore()` to roll back changes to the project library and revert to the known good state recorded in your lockfile.
If you need to roll back to an even older version, take a look at `renv::history()` and `renv::revert()`.

`renv::update()` will also update renv itself, ensuring that you get all the latest features.
See `renv::upgrade()` if you ever want to upgrade just renv, or you need to install a development version from GitHub.

## Infrastructure

Now that you've got the basic usage of renv under your belt, it's time to learn a bit more about how the lockfile works.
You won't typically edit this file directly, but you'll see it changing in your git commits, so it's good to have a sense for what it looks like.

The lockfile is always called `renv.lock` and is a json file that records all the information needed to recreate your project in the future.
Here's an example lockfile, with the markdown package installed from CRAN and the mime package installed from GitHub:

```json
{
  "R": {
    "Version": "`r getRversion()`",
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "https://cloud.r-project.org"
      }
    ]
  },
  "Packages": {
    "markdown": {
      "Package": "markdown",
      "Version": "1.0",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "Hash": "4584a57f565dd7987d59dda3a02cfb41"
    },
    "mime": {
      "Package": "mime",
      "Version": "0.12.1",
      "Source": "GitHub",
      "RemoteType": "github",
      "RemoteHost": "api.github.com",
      "RemoteUsername": "yihui",
      "RemoteRepo": "mime",
      "RemoteRef": "main",
      "RemoteSha": "1763e0dcb72fb58d97bab97bb834fc71f1e012bc",
      "Requirements": [
        "tools"
      ],
      "Hash": "c2772b6269924dad6784aaa1d99dbb86"
    }
  }
}
```

As you can see the json file has two main components: `R` and `Packages`.
The `R` component contains the version of R used, and a list of repositories where packages were installed from.
The `Packages` contains one record for each package used by the project, including all the details needed to re-install that exact version.
The fields written into each package record are derived from the installed package's `DESCRIPTION` file, and include the data required to recreate installation, regardless of whether the package was installed from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/), [Bioconductor](https://www.bioconductor.org/), [GitHub](https://github.com/), [Gitlab](https://about.gitlab.com/), [Bitbucket](https://bitbucket.org/), or elsewhere.
You can learn more about the sources renv supports in `vignette("package-sources")`.

## Caveats

It is important to emphasize that renv is not a panacea for reproducibility.
Rather, it is a tool that can help make projects reproducible by helping with one part of the overall problem: R packages.
There are a number of other pieces that renv doesn't currently provide much help with:

-   **R version**: renv tracks, but doesn't help with, the version of R used with the project. renv can't easily help with this because it's run inside of R, but you might find tools like [rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig) helpful, as they make it easier to switch between multiple version of R on one computer.
-   **Pandoc**: The rmarkdown package relies heavily on [pandoc](https://pandoc.org/), but pandoc is not bundled with the rmarkdown package. That means restoring rmarkdown from the lockfile is insufficient to guarantee exactly the same rendering of RMarkdown documents. If this causes problems for you, you might find the tools provided by the [pandoc package](https://cderv.github.io/pandoc/) to be useful.
-   **Operating system, versions of system libraries, compiler versions**: Keeping a 'stable' machine image is a separate challenge, but [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) is one popular solution. See `vignette("docker", package = "renv")` for recommendations on how Docker can be used together with renv.

You also need to be aware that package installation may fail if a package was originally installed through a binary, but that binary is no longer available.
renv will attempt to install the package from source, but this can (and often will) fail due to missing system prerequisites.

Ultimately, making a project reproducible will always require thought, not just mechanical usage of a tool: what does it mean for a particular project to be reproducible, and how can you use tools to meet that particular goal of reproducibility?

## Uninstalling renv

If you find renv isn't the right fit for your project, deactivating and uninstalling it is easy.

-   To deactivate renv in a project, use `renv::deactivate()`.
    This removes the renv auto-loader from the project `.Rprofile`, but doesn't touch any other renv files used in the project.
    If you'd like to later re-activate renv, you can do so with `renv::activate()`.

-   To completely remove renv from a project, call `renv::deactivate(clean = TRUE)`.
    If you later want to use renv for this project, you'll need to start from scratch with `renv::init().`

If you want to stop using renv for all your projects, you'll also want to remove `renv'`s global infrastructure with the following R code[^6]:

[^6]: If you've customized any of renv's infrastructure paths as described in `?renv::paths`, then you'll need to find and remove those customized folders as well.

```{r}
root <- renv::paths$root()
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
```

You can then uninstall the renv package with `utils::remove.packages("renv")`.

title: "Using renv with Posit Connect"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Using renv with Posit Connect}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}

editor_options: 
  markdown: 
    wrap: 72
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE

```

[Posit Connect](https://posit.co/products/enterprise/connect) is a publication
platform for deploying content built in R and Python to share with a broad
audience. R users may want to develop content (like [Shiny
applications](https://shiny.posit.co/) or [RMarkdown
documents](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/index.html)) using renv and then
publish that content to Posit Connect. This is a supported pattern where
renv is used to manage the local project environment and then Posit Connect
recreates and manages the deployment environment.

## Publishing from the RStudio IDE

The RStudio IDE includes a button for push-button deployment to Posit
Connect: ![RStudio IDE Publish Button](ide-publish.png)

When this option is used to deploy content to Posit Connect, a manifest file
is automatically generated and sent to Posit Connect describing the project
environment. This manifest file will reflect the project environment create and
managed by renv. The renv generated `.Rprofile` file should **not** be
included in deployments to Posit Connect.

## Publishing programatically

When publishing content to Posit Connect programatically, it is necessary to
generate a manifest file describing the project environment. This can be done
with the `writeManifest()` function from the
[rsconnect](https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect) package. When using renv,
the only thing that needs to be considered is that rsconnect should be
installed and executed from within the renv environment so that it recognizes
the local project library when generating the manifest file. As long as
rsconnect is run from within the renv created environment, it will capture
project dependencies from the local renv library. This can be accomplished by
opening the project in RStudio or by starting the R session from the project
root directory. The renv generated `.Rprofile` file should **not** be
included in deployments to Posit Connect.

## A word about packrat

Posit Connect uses [packrat](https://rstudio.github.io/packrat/) to restore
project environments on the Posit Connect server. This should have no impact
on how the user develops content for Posit Connect. It is not necessary for
the user to use packrat instead of renv when developing content, as the
environment management tool used locally has no impact on the tools RStudio
Connect uses for environment management. Therefore, there should be no concerns
with using renv to develop content that will be deployed to Posit Connect.

name: renv/library/macos/R-4.6/aarch64-apple-darwin23/renv/resources/WELCOME
content:
renv: Project Environments for R

Welcome to renv! It looks like this is your first time using renv.
This is a one-time message, briefly describing some of renv's functionality.

renv will write to files within the active project folder, including:

  - A folder 'renv' in the project directory, and
  - A lockfile called 'renv.lock' in the project directory.

In particular, projects using renv will normally use a private, per-project
R library, in which new packages will be installed. This project library is
isolated from other R libraries on your system.

In addition, renv will update files within your project directory, including:

  - .gitignore
  - .Rbuildignore
  - .Rprofile

Finally, renv maintains a local cache of data on the filesystem, located at:

  - ${RENV_PATHS_ROOT}

This path can be customized: please see the documentation in `?renv::paths`.

Please read the introduction vignette with `vignette("renv")` for more information.
You can browse the package documentation online at https://rstudio.github.io/renv/.

content:
renv <- new.env(parent = new.env())

renv$initialize <- function(libname, pkgname) {

  # set up renv + imports environments
  attr(renv, "name") <- "embedded:renv"
  attr(parent.env(renv), "name") <- "imports:renv"

  # get imports
  imports <- ..imports..

  # load the imports required by renv
  for (package in names(imports)) {
    namespace <- asNamespace(package)
    functions <- imports[[package]]
    list2env(mget(functions, envir = namespace), envir = parent.env(renv))
  }

  # source renv into the aforementioned environment
  script <- system.file("vendor/renv.R", package = .packageName)
  sys.source(script, envir = renv)

  # initialize metadata
  renv$the$metadata <- ..metadata..

  # run our load / attach hooks so internal state is initialized
  renv$.onLoad(libname, pkgname)

  # remove our initialize method when we're done
  rm(list = "initialize", envir = renv)

}

# Cache behaviour. Uses the fast "bundled" source, a temporary cache folder,
# a throw-away memory cache and a throw-away "global" environment.

load_quiet <- function(...) {
  msgs <- character(0)
  res <- withCallingHandlers(
    load_teal_neue_data(...),
    message = function(m) {
      msgs <<- c(msgs, conditionMessage(m))
      invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
    }
  )
  list(result = res, messages = paste(msgs, collapse = "\n"))
}

test_that("first load builds from the source, then memory, then disk cache", {
  local_teal_neue_options()
  cache_dir <- getOption("teal_neue.cache_dir")
  mem <- new.env()

  first <- load_quiet(memory_env = mem, cache_dir = cache_dir)
  expect_match(first$messages, "bundled source \\(fresh")
  expect_true(file.exists(file.path(cache_dir, "teal_neue_adam.rds")))
  expect_true(exists("data_cache", envir = mem, inherits = FALSE))

  second <- load_quiet(memory_env = mem, cache_dir = cache_dir)
  expect_match(second$messages, "session memory cache")
  expect_identical(second$result$datasets, first$result$datasets)

  third <- load_quiet(memory_env = new.env(), cache_dir = cache_dir)
  expect_match(third$messages, "disk cache")
  expect_identical(third$result$datasets, first$result$datasets)
})

test_that("the default memory cache lives in the package, not the Global Environment", {
  local_teal_neue_options()
  global_before <- ls(globalenv(), all.names = TRUE)
  load_quiet()
  expect_true(exists("data_cache", envir = the, inherits = FALSE))
  # (.Random.seed may appear: the ADEX pre-processing sets a seed, as in the template)
  expect_identical(setdiff(ls(globalenv(), all.names = TRUE), c(global_before, ".Random.seed")), character(0))
})

test_that("result carries datasets, metadata, source settings and signature", {
  local_teal_neue_options()
  res <- load_quiet(memory_env = new.env())$result
  expect_named(res, c("datasets", "meta", "source", "signature", "created"), ignore.order = TRUE)
  expect_identical(res$source$source, "bundled")
  expect_identical(res$signature, teal_neue_data_signature(teal_neue_source_config("bundled")))
})

test_that("refresh = TRUE rebuilds even with a valid cache", {
  local_teal_neue_options()
  mem <- new.env()
  load_quiet(memory_env = mem)
  again <- load_quiet(memory_env = mem, refresh = TRUE)
  expect_match(again$messages, "fresh")
})

test_that("use_cache = FALSE neither reads nor writes caches", {
  local_teal_neue_options()
  cache_dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
  mem <- new.env()
  res <- load_quiet(memory_env = mem, cache_dir = cache_dir, use_cache = FALSE)
  expect_match(res$messages, "fresh")
  expect_false(file.exists(file.path(cache_dir, "teal_neue_adam.rds")))
  expect_false(exists("data_cache", envir = mem, inherits = FALSE))
})

test_that("a corrupted cache file is ignored and rebuilt", {
  local_teal_neue_options()
  cache_dir <- getOption("teal_neue.cache_dir")
  writeLines("not an rds file", file.path(cache_dir, "teal_neue_adam.rds"))
  res <- load_quiet(memory_env = new.env(), cache_dir = cache_dir)
  expect_match(res$messages, "fresh")
  expect_type(readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "teal_neue_adam.rds")), "list")
})

test_that("a stale cache (different signature) is not used", {
  local_teal_neue_options()
  cache_dir <- getOption("teal_neue.cache_dir")
  mem <- new.env()
  load_quiet(memory_env = mem, cache_dir = cache_dir)
  stale <- get("data_cache", envir = mem)
  stale$signature <- "old"
  assign("data_cache", stale, envir = mem)
  saveRDS(stale, file.path(cache_dir, "teal_neue_adam.rds"))
  res <- load_quiet(memory_env = mem, cache_dir = cache_dir)
  expect_match(res$messages, "fresh")
})

test_that("cache_global copies every dataset; teal_neue_clear_cache removes them", {
  local_teal_neue_options()
  cache_dir <- getOption("teal_neue.cache_dir")
  mem <- new.env()
  glob <- new.env()
  res <- load_quiet(memory_env = mem, global_env = glob, cache_dir = cache_dir, cache_global = TRUE)
  expect_match(res$messages, "available in the Global Environment")
  for (ds in names(res$result$datasets)) {
    expect_identical(get(ds, envir = glob), res$result$datasets[[ds]], info = ds)
  }
  teal_neue_clear_cache(cache_dir = cache_dir, remove_global_datasets = TRUE, global_env = glob, memory_env = mem)
  expect_length(ls(glob, all.names = TRUE), 0)
  expect_length(ls(mem, all.names = TRUE), 0)
  expect_false(file.exists(file.path(cache_dir, "teal_neue_adam.rds")))
})

test_that("the cache signature tracks code and data-source changes", {
  bundled <- teal_neue_data_signature(teal_neue_source_config("bundled"))
  expect_identical(bundled, teal_neue_data_signature(teal_neue_source_config("bundled")))

  s1 <- teal_neue_data_signature(teal_neue_source_config("synthetic", list(N = 50, seed = 1)))
  s2 <- teal_neue_data_signature(teal_neue_source_config("synthetic", list(N = 50, seed = 2)))
  s3 <- teal_neue_data_signature(teal_neue_source_config("synthetic", list(N = 60, seed = 1)))
  expect_length(unique(c(bundled, s1, s2, s3)), 4)

  # a change in the data-producing code gives a different fingerprint
  expect_false(identical(
    bundled,
    teal_neue_data_signature(teal_neue_source_config("bundled"), code = "changed code")
  ))
})

test_that("the code fingerprint covers the pipeline functions and is stable", {
  expect_identical(teal_neue_code_fingerprint(), teal_neue_code_fingerprint())
  expect_type(teal_neue_code_fingerprint(), "character")
})

test_that("the parquet signature changes when a file is added or modified", {
  dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
  writeLines("a", file.path(dir, "adsl.parquet"))
  cfg <- teal_neue_source_config("parquet", parquet_dir = dir)
  before <- teal_neue_data_signature(cfg)
  expect_identical(before, teal_neue_data_signature(cfg))

  writeLines("b", file.path(dir, "adae.parquet"))
  added <- teal_neue_data_signature(cfg)
  expect_false(identical(before, added))

  writeLines("longer content", file.path(dir, "adsl.parquet"))
  modified <- teal_neue_data_signature(cfg)
  expect_false(identical(added, modified))

  # non-ADaM files in the folder do not invalidate the cache
  writeLines("ignored", file.path(dir, "notes.txt"))
  expect_identical(teal_neue_data_signature(cfg), modified)
})

test_that("synthetic source runs end-to-end through the pipeline", {
  local_teal_neue_options()
  res <- load_quiet(source = "synthetic", synthetic = list(N = 30, seed = 11), memory_env = new.env())
  expect_match(res$messages, "synthetic source")
  expect_identical(nrow(res$result$datasets$ADSL), 30L)
  expect_identical(res$result$source$synthetic$seed, 11L)
})

test_that("parquet source runs end-to-end through the pipeline", {
  skip_if_not_installed("arrow")
  local_teal_neue_options()
  dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
  export_adam_parquet(ingest_bundled(), dir)
  res <- load_quiet(source = "parquet", parquet_dir = dir, memory_env = new.env())
  expect_match(res$messages, "parquet source")
  direct <- load_quiet(source = "bundled", memory_env = new.env(), use_cache = FALSE)$result
  for (ds in names(direct$datasets)) {
    expect_equal(as.data.frame(res$result$datasets[[ds]]), as.data.frame(direct$datasets[[ds]]),
                 ignore_attr = TRUE, info = ds)
  }
})

# Look and feel: static assets, options, header/footer, plot defaults. www <- function(...) file.path(teal_neue_www(), ...) # ---- Static assets -------------------------------------------------------------- css_text <- function() paste(readLines(www("teal_neue.css"), warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n") mode_block <- function(css, mode) { pattern <- if (identical(mode, "dark")) 'html\\[data-bs-theme="dark"\\] \\{[^}]+\\}' else 'html:not\\(\\[data-bs-theme="dark"\\]\\) \\{[^}]+\\}' regmatches(css, regexpr(pattern, css)) } test_that("all static assets are installed", { for (f in c("teal_neue.css", "teal_neue.js", "tlg_catalog.css", "tlg_catalog.js", "logo.svg", "favicon.png", "fonts/InterVariable.woff2", "fonts/JetBrainsMonoNL-Regular.woff2", "fonts/JetBrainsMonoNL-Bold.woff2", "fonts/OFL.txt")) { expect_true(file.exists(www(f)), info = f) } }) test_that("fonts are real WOFF2 files and nothing loads from other servers", { css <- css_text() urls <- regmatches(css, gregexpr('url\\("[^"]+"\\)', css))[[1]] urls <- gsub('^url\\("|"\\)$', "", urls) urls <- urls[!startsWith(urls, "data:")] # inline icons expect_setequal(urls, c("fonts/InterVariable.woff2", "fonts/JetBrainsMonoNL-Regular.woff2", "fonts/JetBrainsMonoNL-Bold.woff2")) for (u in urls) expect_identical(readBin(www(u), "raw", 4), charToRaw("wOF2"), info = u) expect_no_match(css, "url\\(\\s*[\"']?(https?:)?//") expect_no_match(css, "@import", fixed = TRUE) # the system font comes first, so Apple devices download nothing expect_match(css, "--tn-font-sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \"Inter\"", fixed = TRUE) ofl <- readLines(www("fonts", "OFL.txt"), warn = FALSE) expect_true(any(grepl("SIL OPEN FONT LICENSE Version 1.1", ofl, fixed = TRUE))) expect_false(any(grepl("Roboto", ofl, fixed = TRUE))) }) test_that("light and dark palettes define the instrument tokens and Bootstrap's colours", { css <- css_text() for (mode in c("light", "dark")) { block <- mode_block(css, mode) expect_length(block, 1) for (token in c("--tn-canvas", "--tn-dot", "--tn-panel", "--tn-panel-2", "--tn-line", "--tn-ink", "--tn-ink-3", "--tn-accent", "--tn-accent-rgb", "--tn-accent-soft", "--tn-signal", "--tn-code-bg", "--bs-body-bg", "--bs-body-color", "--bs-primary", "--bs-link-color", "--bs-border-color")) { expect_match(block, paste0(token, ":"), fixed = TRUE, info = paste(mode, token)) } } expect_match(mode_block(css, "dark"), "color-scheme: dark;", fixed = TRUE) # appearance settings and section tints redefine the tokens for (x in c('html[data-tn-density="compact"] {', 'html[data-tn-density="roomy"] {', 'html[data-tn-text="xl"]', 'html[data-tn-corners="crisp"]', 'html[data-tn-contrast="high"]', 'html[data-tn-canvas="plain"]', '[data-tn-section="safety"]', '[data-tn-section="efficacy"]', '[data-tn-section="explore"]', '[data-tn-section="catalog"]', 'html[data-tn-accent="ocean"]')) { expect_match(css, x, fixed = TRUE, info = x) } }) test_that("the interactive layer and the TLG pages are styled; drawing stays cheap", { css <- css_text() for (x in c(".tn-header {", ".tn-crumbs", ".tn-cmd", ".tn-status-time", ".nav.tn-rail::after", ".tn-pal-item", ".tn-keys", ".tn-tools", ".tn-viewer", ".tn-swipe-handle", ".tn-diff", ".tn-tray", ".tn-where", ".tn-appear", ".tn-seg", ".tn-toast", ".tn-ov-kpi", ".tn-ov-km", ".tn-ov-dumb", ".tn-tip", "html.tn-focus", ".tn-progress", "html .tn-tlg-item.active", "html.tn-still", "@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)", "::view-transition-new(root)")) { expect_match(css, x, fixed = TRUE, info = x) } # no blur, no ambient animation, no background images other than inline SVG expect_no_match(css, "backdrop-filter") expect_no_match(css, "infinite alternate") }) test_that("the script is self-contained and wires every feature", { js <- paste(readLines(www("teal_neue.js"), warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n") expect_no_match(js, "https?://") # no remote code or assets expect_no_match(js, "\\beval\\(") # no eval for (x in c("startViewTransition", "shiny:busy", "shiny:idle", "history.pushState", "popstate", "tn-index", "bootstrap.Tab", "ClipboardItem", "init.dt", "prefers-reduced-motion")) { expect_match(js, x, fixed = TRUE, info = x) } # every action of the command bar has a key, and the keys are handled keys <- regmatches(js, gregexpr('keys: \\["[^"]+"\\]', js))[[1]] expect_gte(length(keys), 10) }) test_that("favicon is an inlined PNG (no request to an external server)", { uri <- teal_neue_favicon() expect_match(uri, "^data:image/png;base64,") png <- jsonlite::base64_dec(sub("^data:image/png;base64,", "", uri)) expect_identical(png[2:4], charToRaw("PNG")) }) # ---- Options ------------------------------------------------------------------------ test_that("look-and-feel options are validated", { expect_true(teal_neue_style_enabled(TRUE)) expect_false(teal_neue_style_enabled(FALSE)) expect_error(teal_neue_style_enabled("yes"), "TRUE or FALSE") for (m in c("auto", "light", "dark")) expect_identical(teal_neue_color_mode(m), m) withr::with_options(list(teal_neue.color_mode = NULL), expect_identical(teal_neue_color_mode(), "light")) withr::with_options(list(teal_neue.ggtheme = NULL), expect_identical(teal_neue_ggtheme(), "minimal")) expect_error(teal_neue_color_mode("sepia"), "teal_neue.color_mode") expect_true(teal_neue_motion(TRUE)) expect_false(teal_neue_motion(FALSE)) withr::with_options(list(teal_neue.motion = NULL), expect_true(teal_neue_motion())) expect_error(teal_neue_motion("slow"), "teal_neue.motion") expect_identical(teal_neue_ggtheme("minimal"), "minimal") expect_null(teal_neue_ggtheme(NULL)) expect_error(teal_neue_ggtheme("excel"), "teal_neue.ggtheme") }) # ---- Header, footer, colour mode ------------------------------------------------------- test_that("the head script carries the colour mode and applies dark mode early", { for (m in c("auto", "light", "dark")) { js <- teal_neue_head_script(m) expect_match(js, sprintf('colorMode:"%s"', m), fixed = TRUE) expect_match(js, "^$") expect_identical(lengths(regmatches(js, gregexpr("", js, fixed = TRUE))), 1L) } # "light" is never pre-set in (bslib's toggle mishandles it; see teal_neue.js) expect_no_match(teal_neue_head_script("light"), "setAttribute('data-bs-theme','light')", fixed = TRUE) # animations: on by default, turned off before the first paint if not wanted expect_match(teal_neue_head_script("light", TRUE), "motion:true", fixed = TRUE) expect_no_match(teal_neue_head_script("light", TRUE), "document.documentElement.classList.add('tn-still')", fixed = TRUE) expect_match(teal_neue_head_script("light", FALSE), "motion:false", fixed = TRUE) expect_match(teal_neue_head_script("light", FALSE), "classList.add('tn-still')", fixed = TRUE) # the saved appearance is applied before the first paint too js <- teal_neue_head_script("light") for (x in c("teal_neue:appearance", "data-tn-text", "data-tn-density", "data-tn-accent", "data-tn-corners", "data-tn-contrast", "data-tn-canvas")) { expect_match(js, x, fixed = TRUE, info = x) } # a saved "auto" colour mode follows the operating system expect_match(js, "m!=='auto'", fixed = TRUE) }) test_that("header: brand, breadcrumb, command button, status, switches and the asset dependency", { header <- teal_neue_header("random.cdisc.data (bundled) \u00b7 400 subjects", style = TRUE) rendered <- htmltools::renderTags(header) expect_match(rendered$html, '
', fixed = TRUE) # the brand is a link home expect_match(rendered$html, '', fixed = TRUE) expect_match(rendered$html, 'data-tn-action="palette"', fixed = TRUE) expect_match(rendered$html, 'data-tn-action="appearance"', fixed = TRUE) # the status shows the source and the number of subjects as a figure expect_match(rendered$html, 'random.cdisc.data (bundled)', fixed = TRUE) expect_match(rendered$html, '400', fixed = TRUE) expect_match(rendered$html, 'subjects', fixed = TRUE) expect_match(rendered$html, "teal_neue_dark_mode", fixed = TRUE) dep <- Filter(function(d) identical(d$name, "teal-neue"), rendered$dependencies) expect_length(dep, 1) expect_identical(dep[[1]]$stylesheet, "teal_neue.css") expect_identical(dep[[1]]$script$src, "teal_neue.js") expect_true("defer" %in% names(dep[[1]]$script)) # never delays the first paint expect_match(dep[[1]]$head, "tealNeue", fixed = TRUE) # a label without a figure is shown as is; no status without a label html <- htmltools::renderTags(teal_neue_header("random.cdisc.data (bundled)", style = TRUE))$html expect_match(html, 'random.cdisc.data (bundled)', fixed = TRUE) expect_no_match(html, "tn-status-figure", fixed = TRUE) expect_no_match(htmltools::renderTags(teal_neue_header(NULL, style = TRUE))$html, "tn-status", fixed = TRUE) # the index travels as JSON, safe inside B"), kind = "table")), tlg = list()) html <- htmltools::renderTags(teal_neue_header("x", style = TRUE, index = idx))$html expect_match(html, '", fixed = TRUE) json <- sub('.*.*', "\\1", html) expect_identical(jsonlite::fromJSON(json, simplifyVector = FALSE)$modules[[1]]$path[[1]], "A B") }) test_that("the module index lists every module with its path and kind, and every TLG output", { fake_module <- function(label) structure(list(label = label), class = "teal_module") fake_modules <- function(label, ...) structure(list(label = label, children = list(...)), class = "teal_modules") mods <- fake_modules( "root", fake_module("App Info"), fake_module("Data Table"), fake_modules("TLG Catalog", fake_module("Adverse Events")), fake_modules("Safety Analysis", fake_modules("Adverse Events", fake_module("AE Summary")), fake_module("Line Plot")) ) catalog <- list(AET01 = list(id = "AET01", title = "Safety Summary", type = "Table", topic = "Adverse Events")) idx <- teal_neue_index(mods, catalog = catalog) paths <- vapply(idx$modules, function(m) paste(unlist(m$path), collapse = " / "), character(1)) expect_identical(paths, c("App Info", "Data Table", "TLG Catalog / Adverse Events", "Safety Analysis / Adverse Events / AE Summary", "Safety Analysis / Line Plot")) kinds <- vapply(idx$modules, `[[`, character(1), "kind") expect_identical(kinds, c("info", "data", "catalog", "table", "graph")) expect_identical(idx$tlg[[1]], list(id = "AET01", title = "Safety Summary", type = "Table", topic = "Adverse Events")) # single paths stay arrays in JSON expect_match(as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(idx, auto_unbox = TRUE)), '"path":["App Info"]', fixed = TRUE) }) test_that("module kinds follow the label", { expect_identical(teal_neue_module_kind("Kaplan Meier Plot"), "graph") expect_identical(teal_neue_module_kind("Regression"), "graph") expect_identical(teal_neue_module_kind("Cox Reg"), "table") expect_identical(teal_neue_module_kind("Variable Browser"), "data") expect_identical(teal_neue_module_kind("Deaths", "TLG Catalog"), "catalog") }) test_that("the plain header (style = FALSE) has no teal_neue assets", { rendered <- htmltools::renderTags(teal_neue_header("x", style = FALSE)) expect_match(rendered$html, "teal_neue: Clinical Trial Analysis", fixed = TRUE) expect_match(rendered$html, "teal_neue_dark_mode", fixed = TRUE) expect_false("teal-neue" %in% vapply(rendered$dependencies, function(d) d$name, character(1))) }) test_that("the footer credits teal and the three templates", { for (style in c(TRUE, FALSE)) { html <- as.character(teal_neue_footer(style = style)) for (x in c("teal", "Exploratory", "Safety", "Efficacy")) expect_match(html, x, fixed = TRUE) } expect_match(as.character(teal_neue_footer(style = TRUE)), paste("teal_neue", teal_neue_version()), fixed = TRUE) expect_match(as.character(teal_neue_footer(style = TRUE)), "tn-footer-keys", fixed = TRUE) }) test_that("the data status describes every source", { expect_identical( teal_neue_data_label(list(source = "bundled"), 400), "random.cdisc.data (bundled) \u00b7 400 subjects" ) expect_match(teal_neue_data_label(list(source = "synthetic", synthetic = list(N = 20, seed = 7)), 20), "seed 7") expect_match(teal_neue_data_label(list(source = "parquet", parquet_dir = "/data/adam"), 1234), "Parquet: adam \u00b7 1,234 subjects") expect_identical(teal_neue_data_label(list(source = "bundled")), "random.cdisc.data (bundled)") }) # ---- Plot defaults ----------------------------------------------------------------------- test_that("plot theme arguments are valid ggplot2 theme settings and render", { skip_if_not_installed("ggplot2") withr::local_pdf(NULL) # draw off-screen, no Rplots.pdf args <- teal_neue_plot_theme_args() expect_true(all(names(args) %in% methods::formalArgs(ggplot2::theme))) # quoted calls, so "Show R code" prints readable code expect_true(all(vapply(args, function(x) is.character(x) || is.call(x), logical(1)))) # built the way teal.widgets builds it: ggplot2::theme() as a call theme_call <- as.call(c(list(quote(ggplot2::theme)), args)) expect_no_error(eval(parse(text = paste(deparse(theme_call), collapse = "\n")))) plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) + ggplot2::geom_point() + ggplot2::facet_wrap(~cyl) + ggplot2::labs(title = "t", subtitle = "s", caption = "NEST PROJECT") + ggplot2::theme_light() + eval(theme_call) expect_no_error(ggplot2::ggplotGrob(plot)) }) test_that("teal.ggplot2_args: caption always, refinements only with the teal_neue style", { skip_if_not_installed("teal.widgets") modern <- teal_neue_ggplot2_args(style = TRUE) plain <- teal_neue_ggplot2_args(style = FALSE) expect_s3_class(modern, "ggplot2_args") expect_identical(modern$labs$caption, "NEST PROJECT") expect_identical(plain$labs$caption, "NEST PROJECT") expect_identical(modern$theme, teal_neue_plot_theme_args()) expect_length(plain$theme, 0) }) test_that("app options: set when unset or ours, never override the user's", { skip_if_not_installed("teal.widgets") mem <- new.env() withr::local_options(teal.ggplot2_args = NULL, shiny.useragg = NULL, teal_neue.style = TRUE) teal_neue_set_app_options(memory_env = mem) expect_identical(getOption("teal.ggplot2_args"), teal_neue_ggplot2_args(style = TRUE)) expect_false(getOption("shiny.useragg")) # an earlier value set by the app is refreshed (e.g. after changing the style) withr::local_options(teal_neue.style = FALSE) teal_neue_set_app_options(memory_env = mem) expect_identical(getOption("teal.ggplot2_args"), teal_neue_ggplot2_args(style = FALSE)) # the user's own value is left alone mine <- teal.widgets::ggplot2_args(labs = list(caption = "MY STUDY")) withr::local_options(teal.ggplot2_args = mine, shiny.useragg = TRUE) teal_neue_set_app_options(memory_env = mem) expect_identical(getOption("teal.ggplot2_args"), mine) expect_true(getOption("shiny.useragg")) }) test_that("module theme arguments are only added where the module supports them", { with_ggtheme <- function(label, ggtheme = c("gray", "bw", "light", "minimal")) list(label = label, ggtheme = ggtheme) association <- function(label, distribution_theme = c("gray", "light"), association_theme = c("gray", "light")) NULL other_choices <- function(label, ggtheme = c("gray", "bw")) NULL no_theme <- function(label, x) NULL expect_identical(teal_neue_theme_args(with_ggtheme, "light"), list(ggtheme = "light")) expect_identical(teal_neue_theme_args(association, "light"), list(distribution_theme = "light", association_theme = "light")) expect_identical(teal_neue_theme_args(other_choices, "light"), setNames(list(), character(0))) expect_identical(teal_neue_theme_args(no_theme, "light"), setNames(list(), character(0))) expect_identical(teal_neue_theme_args(with_ggtheme, NULL), list()) expect_identical(teal_neue_theme_args(with_ggtheme, "light", exclude = "ggtheme"), setNames(list(), character(0))) # arguments are passed through; an explicit ggtheme wins expect_identical(teal_neue_plot_module(with_ggtheme, "A", ggtheme = "light"), list(label = "A", ggtheme = "light")) expect_identical( teal_neue_plot_module(with_ggtheme, "A", ggtheme = "minimal"), list(label = "A", ggtheme = "minimal") ) expect_identical(teal_neue_plot_module(no_theme, "B", x = 1, ggtheme = "light"), NULL) }) test_that("a deprecated theme argument falls back to the module default, silently", { deprecating <- function(label, ggtheme = c("gray", "light")) { if (!missing(ggtheme)) warning("`ggtheme` is deprecated; use decorators instead.", call. = FALSE) list(label = label, ggtheme = if (missing(ggtheme)) "module default" else ggtheme) } expect_no_warning(res <- teal_neue_plot_module(deprecating, "A", ggtheme = "light")) expect_identical(res, list(label = "A", ggtheme = "module default")) # other warnings are not swallowed noisy <- function(label, ggtheme = c("gray", "light")) { warning("something else") label } expect_warning(teal_neue_plot_module(noisy, "B", ggtheme = "light"), "something else") }) test_that("icons: 16 px line icons drawn in the text colour", { for (name in c("Table", "Listing", "Graph", "code", "external", "search", "warning", "data", "density")) { icon <- as.character(teal_neue_icon(name)) expect_match(icon, 'viewBox="0 0 16 16"', fixed = TRUE, info = name) expect_match(icon, 'stroke="currentColor"', fixed = TRUE, info = name) expect_match(icon, 'aria-hidden="true"', fixed = TRUE, info = name) } })

name: tests/testthat/test-overview.R
content:
# Study overview of the home page (R/overview.R)

tiny_adsl <- function() {
  data.frame(
    USUBJID = sprintf("S%02d", 1:8),
    ARM = factor(rep(c("A: Drug X", "B: Placebo"), each = 4), levels = c("A: Drug X", "B: Placebo")),
    SEX = c("F", "F", "M", "F", "M", "M", "F", "M"),
    AGE = c(21, 34, 35, 47, 52, 38, 29, 61),
    RACE = c("ASIAN", "WHITE", "ASIAN", "BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN", "ASIAN", "WHITE", "ASIAN", NA),
    COUNTRY = c("CHN", "USA", "CHN", "BRA", "CHN", "USA", "JPN", "CHN"),
    SAFFL = c(rep("Y", 7), "N"),
    ITTFL = "Y",
    DTHFL = c("N", "N", "Y", "N", "N", "N", "N", "N"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
tiny_adae <- function() {
  data.frame(
    USUBJID = c("S01", "S01", "S02", "S05", "S05", "S06", "S08"),
    AEDECOD = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Headache", "Headache", "Fatigue", "Nausea", "Headache"),
    AESER = c("Y", "N", "N", "N", "Y", "N", "Y"),
    AETOXGR = c("3", "1", "2", "1", "4", "2", "5"),
    AEACN = c("DRUG WITHDRAWN", "DOSE NOT CHANGED", "DOSE NOT CHANGED", "DOSE NOT CHANGED", "DOSE NOT CHANGED", "DOSE NOT CHANGED", "DRUG WITHDRAWN"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

test_that("Kaplan-Meier estimate: product-limit steps and median", {
  km <- overview_km(time = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), event = c(1, 1, 0, 1, 0))
  s <- vapply(km$curve, `[`, numeric(1), 2)
  t <- vapply(km$curve, `[`, numeric(1), 1)
  # S(1) = 4/5, S(2) = 3/5, S(4) = 3/5 * 1/2
  expect_equal(s[t == 1], .8)
  expect_equal(s[t == 2], .6)
  expect_equal(s[t == 4], .3)
  expect_identical(km$median, 4)
  expect_identical(km$n, 5L)
  expect_identical(km$events, 3L)
  # not reached -> NA (null in JSON)
  expect_true(is.na(overview_km(c(1, 2, 3), c(1, 0, 0))$median))
  # long curves are thinned
  big <- overview_km(1:500, rep(1, 500), max_points = 40)
  expect_lte(length(big$curve), 40)
  expect_null(overview_km(numeric(0), numeric(0)))
})

test_that("Wilson interval", {
  ci <- overview_wilson(8, 10)
  expect_equal(ci, c(49.0, 94.3), tolerance = .1)
  expect_true(all(is.na(overview_wilson(0, 0))))
})

test_that("title case keeps small words and NA", {
  expect_identical(overview_title_case(c("BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN", "WHITE", NA)), c("Black or African American", "White", NA))
})

test_that("population and demographics", {
  o <- teal_neue_overview(tiny_adsl())
  expect_identical(o$population$n, 8L)
  expect_identical(vapply(o$population$arms, `[[`, "", "name"), c("A: Drug X", "B: Placebo"))
  expect_identical(vapply(o$population$arms, `[[`, 1, "n"), c(4, 4))
  expect_identical(o$population$countries, 4L)
  age <- o$demographics$age
  expect_identical(age$median, 36.5)
  expect_identical(sum(vapply(age$bins, `[[`, 1L, "n")), 8L)
  expect_identical(age$bins[[1]]$from, 20)
  sex <- o$demographics$sex
  expect_identical(sex[[1]]$level, "F")
  expect_identical(sex[[1]]$pct, 50)
  expect_identical(o$demographics$race[[1]]$level, "Asian")
  # no AE data: no safety part; no TTE / RS: no efficacy part
  expect_null(o$safety)
  expect_null(o$efficacy)
})

test_that("safety: safety population, subjects per arm and category, top terms", {
  o <- teal_neue_overview(tiny_adsl(), tiny_adae())
  saf <- o$safety
  expect_identical(saf$n, 7L) # S08 is not in the safety population
  ids <- vapply(saf$metrics, `[[`, "", "id")
  expect_identical(ids, c("any", "serious", "grade3", "withdrawn", "death"))
  any <- saf$metrics[[1]]$by_arm
  expect_identical(any[[1]]$n, 2L) # S01, S02
  expect_identical(any[[2]]$n, 2L) # S05, S06 (S08 excluded)
  expect_identical(any[[2]]$pct, 66.7) # of 3 placebo subjects in the safety population
  serious <- saf$metrics[[2]]$by_arm
  expect_identical(c(serious[[1]]$n, serious[[2]]$n), c(1L, 1L))
  grade3 <- saf$metrics[[3]]$by_arm
  expect_identical(c(grade3[[1]]$n, grade3[[2]]$n), c(1L, 1L))
  death <- saf$metrics[[5]]$by_arm
  expect_identical(c(death[[1]]$n, death[[2]]$n), c(1L, 0L))
  expect_identical(saf$terms[[1]]$term, "Headache")
  expect_identical(saf$terms[[1]]$n, 3L)
})

test_that("efficacy: survival by arm and response rate", {
  adsl <- tiny_adsl()
  adtte <- data.frame(USUBJID = adsl$USUBJID, PARAMCD = "OS", PARAM = "Overall Survival",
                      AVAL = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 5, 15, 25, 35), CNSR = c(0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1), AVALU = "DAYS")
  adrs <- data.frame(USUBJID = adsl$USUBJID, PARAMCD = "BESRSPI", PARAM = "Best response",
                     AVALC = c("CR", "PR", "SD", "PD", "CR", "NE", "SD", "PR"))
  o <- teal_neue_overview(adsl, NULL, adtte, adrs)
  sv <- o$efficacy$survival
  expect_identical(sv$param, "OS")
  expect_identical(sv$unit, "days")
  expect_length(sv$arms, 2)
  expect_identical(sv$arms[[1]]$arm, "A: Drug X")
  expect_identical(sv$arms[[1]]$events, 3L)
  expect_identical(sv$overall$n, 8L)
  rs <- o$efficacy$response$arms
  expect_identical(c(rs[[1]]$responders, rs[[2]]$responders), c(2L, 2L))
  expect_identical(rs[[1]]$pct, 50)
  expect_true(rs[[1]]$lo < 50 && rs[[1]]$hi > 50)
})

test_that("a broken part is left out, the rest is kept", {
  adae <- tiny_adae()
  adae$USUBJID <- NULL # unusable
  o <- teal_neue_overview(tiny_adsl(), adae)
  expect_null(o$safety)
  expect_false(is.null(o$demographics))
  expect_null(tryCatch(teal_neue_overview(data.frame(x = 1)), error = function(e) NULL))
})

test_that("the overview travels in the header index as JSON", {
  o <- teal_neue_overview(tiny_adsl(), tiny_adae(), links = list(safety = "AE Summary", efficacy = NULL))
  expect_identical(o$links, list(safety = "AE Summary"))
  idx <- list(modules = list(list(path = list("App Info"), kind = "info")), tlg = list(), overview = o)
  html <- htmltools::renderTags(teal_neue_header("x", style = TRUE, index = idx))$html
  json <- sub('.*<script type="application/json" id="tn-index">(.*?)</script>.*', "\\1", html)
  back <- jsonlite::fromJSON(json, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  expect_identical(back$overview$population$n, 8L)
  expect_identical(back$overview$safety$metrics[[1]]$id, "any")
})

name: tests/testthat/test-preprocess.R
tests/testthat/test-speed.R
content:
# Start-up speed: app cache, page cache, memoised registry

test_that("the page is built once for plain requests, always for requests with a query", {
  n <- 0
  ui <- function(request) {
    n <<- n + 1
    htmltools::div("page", n)
  }
  fast <- teal_neue_fast_ui(ui)
  a <- fast(list(QUERY_STRING = ""))
  b <- fast(list(QUERY_STRING = ""))
  expect_identical(a, b)
  expect_identical(n, 1)
  fast(list(QUERY_STRING = "?_state_id_=abc")) # e.g. a bookmark to restore
  expect_identical(n, 2)
  # switched off with the app cache
  withr::with_options(list(teal_neue.app_cache = FALSE), expect_identical(teal_neue_fast_ui(ui), ui))
  # a static UI is passed through
  tags <- htmltools::div("static")
  expect_identical(teal_neue_fast_ui(tags), tags)
})

test_that("the app cache key follows the settings and can be switched off", {
  skip_if_not_installed("teal.neue")
  k1 <- teal_neue_app_key("bundled", list(), "cache", TRUE)
  expect_type(k1, "character")
  expect_identical(teal_neue_app_key("bundled", list(), "cache", TRUE), k1)
  expect_false(identical(teal_neue_app_key("bundled", list(), "cache", FALSE), k1))
  withr::with_options(list(teal_neue.color_mode = "dark"), expect_false(identical(teal_neue_app_key("bundled", list(), "cache", TRUE), k1)))
  withr::with_options(list(teal_neue.refresh_cache = TRUE), expect_null(teal_neue_app_key("bundled", list(), "cache", TRUE)))
  withr::with_options(list(teal_neue.app_cache = FALSE), expect_null(teal_neue_app_key("bundled", list(), "cache", TRUE)))
})

test_that("the TLG Catalog registry is built once per session", {
  first <- tlg_catalog()
  expect_true(exists("tlg_catalog", envir = the, inherits = FALSE))
  expect_identical(tlg_catalog(), first)
  expect_identical(names(tlg_catalog_build()), names(first))
})

test_that("clearing the cache also forgets the app", {
  mem <- new.env()
  assign("app_cache", list(key = "k", app = list()), envir = mem)
  teal_neue_clear_cache(cache_dir = withr::local_tempdir(), memory_env = mem)
  expect_false(exists("app_cache", envir = mem, inherits = FALSE))
})

name: vignettes/data-sources.Rmd
content:
---
title: "Data sources and the data contract"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Data sources and the data contract}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(teal.neue)
```

## The pipeline

```
 source ──► ingest_adam() ──► validate_adam() ──► preprocess_adam() ──► cache ──► app
 (raw ADaM)   read raw data     data contract       analysis datasets    memory + disk
```

`load_teal_neue_data()` runs the pipeline and returns the 13 analysis-ready
datasets, from cache whenever possible.

## Three data sources

### Bundled (default)

The pre-generated synthetic datasets shipped with *random.cdisc.data*
(`cadsl`, `cadae`, ...). Fast, and always the same data.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
raw <- ingest_adam("bundled")
```

### Freshly generated synthetic data

Generated with the `random.cdisc.data::rad*()` functions. Choose the number
of subjects and the seed; extra arguments can be passed to each generator.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
raw <- ingest_adam(
  "synthetic",
  synthetic = list(
    N = 200,                                  # subjects
    seed = 7,                                 # change for a new draw
    args = list(ADAE = list(max_n_aes = 5))   # per-dataset rad*() arguments
  )
)
```

With `seed = NA` a random seed is drawn once per session, printed in the
console and stored in option `teal_neue.synthetic`, so the app and its "Show R
code" always use the same draw.

### Parquet files

Point `parquet_dir` at a folder with one file per dataset: `adsl.parquet`,
`adae.parquet`, ... (or `adsl_adam.parquet`, ...; case-insensitive). Other files
are ignored; extra ADaM datasets are read but reported as unused. Needs the
*arrow* package.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
raw <- ingest_adam("parquet", parquet_dir = "path/to/adam")
```

`export_adam_parquet()` writes data in that layout, e.g. to freeze a synthetic
draw:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
export_adam_parquet(ingest_adam("synthetic", list(N = 200, seed = 7)), "cache")
run_app(source = "parquet", parquet_dir = "cache")
```

## The data contract

Every source is checked right after ingestion, so data problems are reported
before the app starts instead of failing inside a module. The contract lists
the datasets and columns the app needs:

```{r}
names(adam_contract())
adam_contract()$ADTTE
```

`validate_adam()` stops with the full list of problems (missing datasets or
columns, empty datasets, an ADSL with more than one row per subject) and
warns about subjects that have no ADSL record.

The app's modules also pre-select some values (e.g. the overall survival
parameter `OS`). With real data these may not exist; `check_app_defaults()`
warns about each missing one, so you know which defaults to adjust:

```{r}
adam_app_defaults()[[1]]
```

## Readable adverse event names

*random.cdisc.data* codes the adverse event hierarchy with placeholders
(`"dcd A.1.1.1.1"`). Pre-processing replaces them with illustrative
MedDRA-style names; the mapping is one-to-one per level, so no AE groups are
merged and all counts are unchanged. Real MedDRA terms pass through untouched.

```{r}
head(ae_dictionary(), 4)
decode_ae_terms(data.frame(AEDECOD = c("dcd A.1.1.1.1", "dcd D.1.1.4.2", "Headache")))
```

## Caching

`load_teal_neue_data()` uses the first valid cache:

1. **session memory** - instant for repeated launches in one R session;
2. **disk** - `teal_neue_adam.rds` in `tools::R_user_dir("teal.neue", "cache")`
   (option `teal_neue.cache_dir`);
3. **fresh build** - then cached.

The cache is rebuilt automatically when the package version or any
data-producing function changes, or when the source changes (source type,
synthetic settings, *random.cdisc.data* version, or a parquet file's name,
size or modification time). Force a rebuild with `refresh = TRUE` (option
`teal_neue.refresh_cache`) or clear everything with `teal_neue_clear_cache()`.

## Switching to real study data

1. Export the ADaM datasets as parquet (`adsl.parquet`, ...) into one folder.
2. `run_app(source = "parquet", parquet_dir = "that/folder")`.
3. Fix anything `validate_adam()` reports; review the warnings of
   `check_app_defaults()` and adjust the module defaults if needed.
4. Run the test suite (`devtools::test()`); the data invariants run on every
   data scenario (see `vignette("development", package = "teal.neue")`).

name: vignettes/development.Rmd
content:
---
title: "Development and testing"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Development and testing}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

## Package layout

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `R/ingest.R` | Data sources, parquet import/export, data contract |
| `R/preprocess.R` | Pre-processing per dataset (from the templates) |
| `R/ae_dictionary.R` | Readable adverse event names |
| `R/data_pipeline.R` | `load_teal_neue_data()`: pipeline + caches |
| `R/teal_data.R` | `teal_data` object, reproducible code, join keys |
| `R/app_modules.R` | Module configuration (one function per tab group) |
| `R/app_filters.R` | Module-specific filters / starting populations |
| `R/app_ui.R` | Header (logo, data badge, dark mode toggle), footer, favicon, asset dependency |
| `R/plot_theme.R` | Plot defaults: `teal.ggplot2_args`, default ggplot2 theme of the plot modules |
| `R/tlg_catalog.R` | TLG Catalog module: registry, pages, runner, renderers |
| `R/tlg_entries_*.R` | TLG Catalog outputs (one function per topic group) |
| `R/run_app.R` | `teal_neue_app()`, `run_app()` |
| `R/options.R` | `?teal_neue_options` |
| `inst/www/` | Stylesheets, scripts (colour mode, TLG Catalog list), logo, favicon and fonts |
| `inst/templates/` | The original teal.gallery templates |
| `app.R` | Launcher for RStudio "Run App" / Posit Connect |

## Everyday workflow

```{r}
devtools::load_all()   # load the package from source
run_app()

devtools::document()   # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen comments
devtools::test()       # run the test suite
devtools::check()      # full R CMD check
```

## Adding or changing a module

Modules live in `R/app_modules.R`, in the function of their tab group
(`modules_exploratory()`, `modules_safety()`, `modules_efficacy()`). Keep
labels unique across the app: module-specific filters are keyed by label,
and `teal_neue_modules()` stops if two modules share one. Safety and efficacy
modules automatically get their starting population (see `R/app_filters.R`).

Exploratory plot modules are created with
`teal_neue_plot_module(tm_g_..., <arguments>)` rather than a direct call: it
adds the app's default ggplot2 theme (option `teal_neue.ggtheme`), but only when
the installed module version has a matching theme argument, so a module API
change cannot break the app.

If a new module needs a dataset column that is not yet in the contract, add it
to `adam_contract()`; if it pre-selects a value, add it to
`adam_app_defaults()`.

## Adding or changing a TLG Catalog output

Each output is one `tlg()` entry in `R/tlg_entries_*.R`:

```{r}
tlg("AET02", "Adverse Events", "Table",
    topic = "Adverse Events", slug = "adverse-events",
    data = c("ADSL", "ADAE"),            # app datasets the code uses
    code = r"--(
library(tern)
adsl <- ADSL %>% filter(SAFFL == "Y") %>% df_explicit_na()
...
result <- build_table(lyt, df = adae, alt_counts_df = adsl)
)--")
```

The code is a plain string: it runs with teal's `eval_code()` on the page's
filtered data (datasets in upper case: `ADSL`, `ADAE`, ...) and must create
`result`: an rtables table, an rlistings listing, a data.frame, or a plot
(ggplot2, grid or lattice). The same string is what "Show R code" shows. Use
`teal.neue::tlg_example_data("ADPC", adsl)` (and list the dataset in `extra`)
for datasets the app does not load; list non-default packages in `packages`.

`test-tlg-catalog.R` renders every output on the bundled data and lists the
ones that fail with their error message (skip it with
`Sys.setenv(TEAL_NEUE_SKIP_TLG = "true")`).

## Styling and the interactive layer

The look lives in `inst/www/teal_neue.css` and the behaviour in
`inst/www/teal_neue.js` (no dependencies). `inst/www/tlg_catalog.css` holds
the layout of the TLG Catalog pages only (Bootstrap variables, no colours of
its own); `teal_neue.css` skins those pages in its last section.

The stylesheet redefines Bootstrap's CSS variables on top of teal's default
theme instead of compiling a custom `bslib::bs_theme()`. That keeps bslib's
precompiled CSS (no Sass compilation at start-up) and the app recognisably
teal. Its tokens (`--tn-*`: type scale, spacing, radii, motion, canvas,
panels, lines, ink levels, accent and signal colours) are defined once for
both modes and per mode in the `html:not([data-bs-theme="dark"])` (light) and
`html[data-bs-theme="dark"]` blocks. Appearance settings are attributes on
`<html>` that override tokens (`data-tn-text`, `data-tn-density`,
`data-tn-accent`, `data-tn-corners`, `data-tn-contrast`, `data-tn-canvas`);
the current category is `data-tn-section` (set by the script), which picks
the accent tokens of that category unless a fixed accent is chosen. Guidelines:

* prefer changing a token or a `--bs-*` variable over styling a component;
* dark-mode values go in the `html[data-bs-theme="dark"]` block;
* selectors start with `html` when they must win over widget stylesheets that
  load later (e.g. ionRangeSlider, selectize);
* keep drawing cheap: no `backdrop-filter`, no background images, no
  infinite animations; animate `transform`, `opacity` and colours only;
* entrance animations use `backwards` fill (or end on `none`), so no
  `transform` is left on a surface afterwards;
* never set a font family inside plots (see `R/plot_theme.R`).

`teal_neue.js` works from the page itself, so it does not depend on how teal
builds its navigation:

* **Navigation model**: every Bootstrap tab trigger (`data-bs-toggle="tab"`
  or `"pill"`) and its chain of parent tabs and menus gives the path of a
  view. Opening a view shows each tab of its chain in turn (Bootstrap's Tab
  API). Elements that are not Bootstrap tabs are reached by clicking the
  visible elements labelled with each part of the path.
* **Index**: the header carries a JSON index (`teal_neue_index()` in
  `R/app_ui.R`): the path and kind of every module and the ID, title, type and
  topic of every TLG output. The command bar uses it for order, icons and the
  outputs; without it, it indexes the tabs it finds.
* **Views** are tracked from Bootstrap's `shown.bs.tab` events and clicks on
  tabs and TLG outputs; each view updates the breadcrumb, the page title, the
  address (`history.pushState`, a `#/` path of slugs) and the recent list
  (`localStorage`). On load and on `popstate`, the `#/` path is opened.
* **Status** uses Shiny's `shiny:busy` / `shiny:idle` events.
* **Home page**: the study overview is computed in R when the app is built
  (`teal_neue_app_overview()` in `R/overview.R`: small, JSON-ready summaries,
  each part in its own `tryCatch()`), travels in the index as `overview`,
  and is drawn by the script with HTML and SVG into the App Info page. Arm
  colours are CSS variables (`--tn-arm-0` ... `--tn-arm-5`, `--tn-arm-n` for
  placebo / control), so both colour modes follow.
* **Tools and pins** work on `.shiny-plot-output img` and on HTML tables
  outside DataTables; pins are kept in memory for the session (images as data
  URLs, tables as HTML).
* Settings from R (`teal_neue.color_mode`, `teal_neue.motion`) arrive in
  `window.tealNeue` through the inline script of the header dependency,
  which also applies dark mode and the saved appearance before the first
  paint.
* **Start-up**: `teal_neue_app()` keeps the built app in `the$app_cache`
  (keyed by `teal_neue_app_key()`: package version, data signature, look
  options); `run_app()` wraps teal's UI with `teal_neue_fast_ui()`, which
  serves the first page built for a plain request again. `tlg_catalog()` is
  memoised. The build message breaks the time down by step.

### Fonts

The fonts are subsets converted to WOFF2 with
[fontTools](https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools): Inter (the variable
font, pinned to its text optical size; every weight) and JetBrains Mono
(no-ligature cut). To rebuild them (e.g. for a newer Inter release), keep
Latin, Greek, punctuation, arrows and mathematical operators:

```sh
UNICODES="U+0000-00FF,U+0100-017F,U+0131,U+0152-0153,U+02BB-02BC,U+02C6,U+02DA,U+02DC,U+0370-03FF,U+2000-206F,U+2070-209F,U+20AC,U+2122,U+2190-21FF,U+2200-22FF,U+2300-23FF,U+25A0-25FF,U+2713-2717,U+FEFF,U+FFFD"

fonttools varLib.instancer InterVariable.ttf opsz=14 -o inter-text.ttf
pyftsubset inter-text.ttf --flavor=woff2 --layout-features='*' --no-hinting \
  --desubroutinize --output-file=InterVariable.woff2 --unicodes="$UNICODES"
```

JetBrains Mono uses the same `pyftsubset` command on
`JetBrainsMonoNL-Regular.ttf` and `-Bold.ttf` (no instancer step; the
unicode list adds box drawing, `U+2500-257F`). Licences and copyright notices
are in `inst/www/fonts/OFL.txt` and `inst/COPYRIGHTS`.

## Tests

The suite (`tests/testthat/`) checks every step:

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| `test-ingest.R` | every source, synthetic settings and reproducibility, parquet naming and round trip |
| `test-contract.R` | each rule of the data contract on tiny hand-made data |
| `test-preprocess.R` | invariants of every derived dataset |
| `test-ae-dictionary.R` | AE decoding (one-to-one, unknown codes, labels kept) |
| `test-data-pipeline.R` | memory/disk/fresh caches, refresh, invalidation, global copies |
| `test-teal-data.R` | datasets, join keys, reproducible code, error messages |
| `test-app.R` | app builds without warnings, UI renders, labels, filter mapping, no third-party requests |
| `test-speed.R` | page cache, app cache key, memoised registry, cache clearing |
| `test-overview.R` | the study overview: Kaplan-Meier estimate, Wilson interval, populations, every part, robustness, JSON |
| `test-look.R` | assets and fonts, light and dark tokens, styles of the interactive layer, the script's wiring, options, header/footer, module index, icons, colour-mode script, plot defaults |
| `test-tlg-catalog.R` | TLG Catalog registry, pages, runner, and **every output on the bundled data** |

**Consistency whatever the data.** The data invariants run on several
*different* datasets - the bundled data, two synthetic draws of different size
and seed, and a parquet round trip - so they test properties of the pipeline,
not one snapshot. Run a subset with an environment variable:

```{r}
Sys.setenv(TEAL_NEUE_TEST_SCENARIOS = "bundled")   # quick run
devtools::test()
```

The parquet tests need *arrow* and are skipped without it. Tests use temporary
cache folders and a throw-away memory cache; they never touch your real cache
or Global Environment.

## Deployment

`app.R` at the project root loads the package with `pkgload::load_all()` and
calls `run_app()`, so the project folder can be deployed as a Shiny app
(e.g. `rsconnect::deployApp()`). `R/_disable_autoload.R` stops Shiny from also
sourcing `R/` on its own.

name: vignettes/teal_neue.Rmd
content:
---
title: "Getting started with teal_neue"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Getting started with teal_neue}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

**teal_neue** (R package `teal.neue`) brings the exploratory, safety and
efficacy analyses of a clinical trial together in a single
[teal](https://insightsengineering.github.io/teal/) app. It combines the three
*teal.gallery* templates (kept for reference in `inst/templates/`) on top of a
cached data pipeline, with a modernised but still recognisably teal look.

## Run the app

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(teal.neue)
run_app()
```

From the project folder you can also open `app.R` in RStudio and press
**Run App** (it loads the package with `pkgload` and calls `run_app()`).

The first launch builds the data (a few seconds); later launches in the same
R session are served from memory, and new sessions from the disk cache.

## A tour of the app

| Tab | What it shows | Starting population |
|---|---|---|
| App Info | Sections, data source, packages | - |
| Data Table, Variable Browser | All datasets | All subjects |
| TLG Catalog | Every table, listing and graph of the TLG Catalog, one page per topic | As in the catalog (per output) |
| Exploratory Analysis | Distributions, outliers, associations, regression, PCA, ... | All subjects |
| Safety Analysis | Demographics, adverse events, labs, exposure, vitals, ECG, concomitant medication | Safety population (`SAFFL == "Y"`) |
| Efficacy Analysis | Forest plots, Kaplan-Meier, response, time-to-event, Cox, logistic, MMRM, ANCOVA | Intent-to-treat (`ITTFL == "Y"`) |

* **Filters are module-specific.** Sex and age filters apply everywhere;
  each safety module also starts on the safety population and each efficacy
  module on the intent-to-treat population, exactly as in the source
  templates. Changing a shared filter updates every module that uses it.
* **Show R code** in any module gives runnable code: it starts with
  `teal.neue::load_teal_neue_data()` with the data-source settings written out, so it
  reproduces the same data in a fresh R session.
* **Dark mode**: the sun/moon button in the header switches the whole app
  between light and dark colours. The app starts in light mode, and the
  browser remembers your choice.
* **Header badge**: shows the data source and the number of subjects.

## The TLG Catalog

The **TLG Catalog** tab reproduces the outputs of the
[TLG Catalog](https://insightsengineering.github.io/tlg-catalog/stable/tlg-index.html)
on the app's data: one page per topic (Adverse Events, Concomitant
Medications, Lab Results, Efficacy, Pharmacokinetics, ...), with the tables,
listings and graphs of that topic in a searchable list on the left. Select an
output (click, or use the arrow keys) to compute it on the filtered data.

* **Show R code** gives the complete code: the data loading, the filters and
  the output's code, written in the catalog's style (tern, rtables, rlistings).
* **Catalog page** opens the output's page in the TLG Catalog.
* A few outputs need datasets the app does not load (ADPC, ADPP, ADAB, ADMH,
  ADHY); they use the *random.cdisc.data* examples for the same patients, as
  noted on their page.

## The data in the console

`run_app()` copies every analysis dataset into the Global Environment, so after
closing the app you can explore them directly:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
head(ADSL)
table(ADAE$AEDECOD)
```

Without the app:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
neue <- load_teal_neue_data(cache_global = TRUE)
names(neue$datasets)
```

Turn the copy off with `options(teal_neue.cache_global = FALSE)` or
`run_app(cache_global = FALSE)`.

## Settings

Everything is configured with R options (see `?teal_neue_options`) or the
equivalent arguments of `run_app()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# freshly generated synthetic data: 200 subjects, seed 7
run_app(source = "synthetic", synthetic = list(N = 200, seed = 7))

# your own ADaM data as parquet files
run_app(source = "parquet", parquet_dir = "path/to/adam")

# force a rebuild of the cached data
options(teal_neue.refresh_cache = TRUE)
```

See `vignette("data-sources", package = "teal.neue")` for the data sources, the
data contract and the cache.

## Look and feel

The app keeps teal's structure and its standard Bootstrap 5 theme. A
stylesheet and one script on top of it add:

* **A home page**: click the logo (or press `H`). *Study at a glance*
  summarises the study by arm: key figures, demographics (age, sex, race),
  safety (subjects with any, serious or severe adverse events, deaths, the
  most frequent events) and efficacy (overall survival curves, response
  rates). Point at an arm to highlight it in every widget, hover the
  survival curves to read them at any time, and follow a widget's link to
  the module that goes into detail. These figures describe the whole study,
  before any filter; the modules are where filtered, reproducible analyses
  happen.
* **A command bar**: press `Ctrl+K` (`Cmd+K` on a Mac), `/`, or click the
  search field in the header. Before you type, *Where to?* shows every
  module in its category, nested as in the menus. Type a few letters of a module
  (`km`, `ae grade`), a TLG output ID (`aet02`) or an action (`>dark`).
  `Enter` opens it; `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` opens it in a new browser tab.
* **Where am I**: the header shows the path of the current module (for
  example *Safety Analysis / Adverse Events / AE Summary*); click a part of it
  to see the other modules of that group.
* **Links to every view**: the address bar follows the app
  (`.../#/efficacy-analysis/kaplan-meier-plot`), so views can be bookmarked
  and shared, and the browser's back button goes to the previous view.
* **Output tools**: hover a plot to expand it (zoom with the wheel, drag to
  pan), pin it, compare it, copy it or download it; hover a table to copy it
  for Excel or download it as CSV.
* **Comparison**: pin a plot, change a filter, then choose *Compare*: swipe
  a divider between the two versions, put them side by side, or show their
  difference (what changed keeps its colour, the rest turns white). Pins stay
  in a tray (`P`) for the session.
* **Keyboard shortcuts** for everything; press `?` to see them.
* **A calm, precise look** ("Instrument"): ruled white panels on a dot-grid
  canvas, one teal accent, the system font (Inter elsewhere) for text and
  JetBrains Mono for dataset names, IDs and numbers; a quiet tint per
  category (blue for Exploratory, terracotta for Safety, green for Efficacy,
  violet for the TLG Catalog); a dark mode that works.
* **Appearance** (the sliders button, or `A`): text size, spacing, accent,
  corners, contrast, canvas and motion, remembered by the browser.
* **Plots**: an editorial look for every ggplot2 module (large titles, facet
  labels as headings, a graded ink scale, no tick marks) and
  `theme_minimal()` as the default theme of the exploratory plots. Both are
  applied through teal's own settings, so "Show R code" reproduces the plots
  exactly. In dark mode, plots stay white paper.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(teal_neue.color_mode = "dark")  # default mode for first-time visitors ("light")
options(teal_neue.motion = FALSE)       # no animations
options(teal_neue.ggtheme = "bw")       # another default plot theme (NULL: module defaults)
options(teal_neue.style = FALSE)        # the plain teal look of the source templates
```

To change the plot typography, set teal's own option, which teal_neue then
leaves alone:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(teal.ggplot2_args = teal.widgets::ggplot2_args(
  labs = list(caption = "MY STUDY"),
  theme = teal_neue_plot_theme_args()
))
```
